title: Rival AI agents, Instinct and Meta’s Muse, both add the ability to make calls
content: Disrupt 2026: OpenAI, Anthropic, Replit, and more take over 6 industry stages.25% off tickets now Back by popular demand:Save up to $300 on Disrupt Latest AI Amazon Apps Biotech & Health Climate Cloud Computing Commerce Crypto Enterprise EVs Fintech Fundraising Gadgets Gaming Google Government & Policy Hardware Instagram Layoffs Media & Entertainment Meta Microsoft Privacy Robotics Security Social Space Startups TikTok Transportation Venture Staff Events Startup Battlefield StrictlyVC Newsletters Podcasts Videos Partner Content TechCrunch Brand Studio Contact Us Text-based AI assistants are a hot market, with Instinct, Wajo, Town, Ollie, and Meta’s Muse agent, whichlaunched last week, vying for users’ attention and tasks. San Francisco-basedInstinctis one of the most popular of the lot, attracting huge investor interest at whatis reportedlya $10 billion valuation. Instinct’s popularity may now grow even further, as it’s added a new calling feature that lets your agent place calls and act as a concierge. Meta’s Muse, another serious contender in this battle, has also done the same. Instinct’s founder Noah Shinnannounced on Xthat the buzzy startup’s new calling feature, Instinct Concierge, can do things like book restaurants that don’t take online reservations, get on your dentist’s cancellation list, or sort out problems with your cable bill. The feature is rolling out in early access to some users, with plans to expand to all users in time, he said. Your Instinct can now handle phone calls.Introducing Instinct Concierge – a white glove service meant to handle high-touch cases, such as making phone calls, high-end service booking, and more. You’ll be able to book the restaurant that doesn’t take online reservations, get on…pic.twitter.com/vGVnAJ1MF1 Though Instinct is shipping fast, Meta’s Muse AI assistant is keeping up. It also just gained the ability to place calls to U.S. businesses. The tech giant said the feature will first roll out to users who ask Muse to make a call. (This essentially serves as a feature request mechanism, and Meta said that whenever Muse launches new features, they’ll be available first to people who ask Muse about them.) These calling features arrive as a number of rivals had been touting their ability to make calls as an advantage over Instinct; but with Instinct’s Concierge feature rollout, they’re all now in parity with each other on this front. we just expanded the@Musebeta for outbound calls to US businesses, prioritizing folks who'd asked their Muse to let us know they wanted it first :)if you're in, give it a shot and tell us what you think. phone calling was one of our top requests and your feedback helped make… Last week, Instinct also rolled out email addresses tolet Instinct handle account sign-up and management. The company additionally now allows its users’ assistants to contactother people’s assistantsfor managing certain tasks, by adding those users to a trusted network. Both Instinct and Muse have seen great traction over the last few weeks. Instinct raised$350 million at a $2.5 billion valuation last month, and it is reportedly in talks to raise$1 billion at a $10 billion valuation, with investors showing heavy interest in text-based assistants that can navigate different surfaces for users. Analytics firm Sensor Tower noted that Muse outgrew the Meta AI app launch in the first few days. The app garnered over 730,000 downloads in the U.S., compared to the Meta AI app, which was downloaded 707,000 times post-launch in the first five days.
